poems:
12:00.
The whole building agrees, without a vote, to think about sandwiches.

The deli line develops a hierarchy in under a minute.
Nobody argues with it.
A folded paper bag, grease showing through one corner, on a truck's dashboard.

Peel the lid back halfway.
Stir.
Replace the lid.
Wait one minute.
Stir again.
Eat standing up.

Somebody in the break room microwaved fish.
There will be a memo.
12:05, and the parking lot has quietly become a dining room.

Half the day, spent.
Half, outstanding.
The retired guy at the diner counter orders it, and the waitress writes nothing down.
You have twenty-two minutes and a fork from the drawer nobody has ever organized.

Office fridge, contents:
yogurt, expired.
Yogurt, unlabeled.
One lime.
Four hot sauces.
Somebody's entire Thanksgiving.

12:10.
The morning's plan is now a suggestion.

12:11. Talk radio argues to an empty sedan
parked in the one strip of shade.

12:12.
The one minute of the day that looks like a typo.

Bread, tomato, salt.
That is the whole argument.
Somewhere a bell, somewhere a horn, somewhere a man named Dale unwrapping the same burrito he unwrapped yesterday.
12:15. Half the mail sent this morning was about scheduling this afternoon.
The dog has known since eleven.
Lunch, n. The meeting you are allowed to eat during.

Two hard hats on the tailgate.
Two men on the curb behind the truck, facing the road.

You said you would go outside today.
There is a bench. It has been there the whole time.

12:20. A soda can cracks in a quiet office.
Everyone hears the vacation in it.
The salad was a moral decision made at eight by a person who is not here now.

Ice machine.
Long exhale.
A nurse eats standing at the counter, four bites in, then the phone.

OUT OF ORDER, says the card reader.
CASH ONLY. SORRY.
The sorry underlined twice.
The afternoon is still theoretical.
Somebody's mother calls at this exact minute every weekday, and neither of them can say why it is this one.

12:27. A picnic table claimed by one person,
used entirely.
You will remember, at four o'clock and sharply, that you skipped this.

12:29. A pickle spear, unaccounted for,
claimed at the last moment.

12:30. Half the office eating at a desk,
apologizing to no one.
"No, keep it, I have another one in the truck."
A folding table, a cash box, a hand-lettered sign for tamales, a line eleven people long.

12:33. A dropped tray somewhere in the food court.
Applause, brief, ashamed of itself.

12:34.
Four numbers in a row, once a day, and no witnesses.

You are being paid, right now, to eat this.
Chew slower.

Grill scrape. Ticket printer.
Somebody yelling for hands.
The gas station espresso machine has a sticker on it apologizing for itself.
12:38, and the first person is back at their desk, which the rest of us have noted.
A pigeon has committed to the crust and cannot lift it.
If it is a school day, the cafeteria has reached the volume at which adults stop trying.
Mayonnaise, unforgiven.
Half the floor is walking a loop around the same block and calling it fresh air.

12:43.
A calendar hold titled hold
holds nothing.

Cut it on the diagonal.
It tastes better.
No one has ever explained this.
Third shift sleeps behind blackout curtains while somebody two houses down starts a mower.

Your soup is hotter in the middle.
It has always been hotter in the middle.
A woman in a suit carrying a rotisserie chicken across a parking lot.
12:48. Somebody has decided the afternoon starts at one, and is therefore free for twelve minutes.
Crumbs on the break room table from a cake for a person who left in March.
Napkin dispenser empty in the practiced way.
In the shop the radio is loud and the compressor is louder, and lunch is a sandwich on a fender.
A red thermos, dented, upright in the grass.

12:53.
Somebody is chewing on mute.
Hospital cafeteria. Scrubs, visitors, and one man in a tie eating alone, very fast.

12:55. Umbrellas in the lobby stand,
a parliament of the unprepared.

12:56. In the elevator back up,
lunch already a rumor.
Somebody folds the bag over twice and writes their name on it with the pen they use for everything.

12:58.
The plastic fork snaps at the base, as designed.

Last minute of noon.
Everything after this is afternoon, which is a longer word for a reason.
